transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-30
Time: 15:00 PST (48m)
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood), Priya Patel (Redwood), Liam O'Connor (Auriga), Maya Chen (Auriga), Noah Rivera (Auriga)

Auto-generated summary:
- Quick discovery focused on self-serve credits and first-call velocity, plus hosting fit (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Action: Redwood to run a small bench and send pricing + credits.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits
- Time-to-first-API-call (first inference) and sample latency expectations
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria (cost, latency, security)
- Next steps: bench + security docs + prompt set

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm joined by priya who is our systems engineer for inference, thanks for taking the time
[00:07] Liam: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we wanted to do a quick run through — we're trying to figure out how fast we can get something demoable using your API versus pushing for dedicated infra.
[00:16] Maya: and also want to be clear on data residency, like our PII flow.
[00:20] Priya: totally — quick note, in the self-serve hosted flow you can get started in minutes, we give free credits for a trial, and many teams hit a first request in under 10 minutes from signup. though iff you have strict residency we can discuss Private/VPC.
[00:35] Noah: when you say "first request in 10 minutes" is that with a ready model, or do you need custom weights?
[00:40] Jordan: it's with our hosted API and a model from our catalog — so out of box, yes. if you need a custom model or a large private dataset then that adds onboarding time.
[00:48] Liam: our ideal pilot is 5–10 qps, latency sub-200ms p50 for chat-style completions, cost under a threshold — does that profile map to hosted or dedicated?
[00:57] Priya: good question. 5–10 qps is modest, hosted can absolutely handle it with the right model variant — the tradeoff is single-tenant predictability. dedicated gives you reserved throughput and slightly more predictable tail latency, plus tenancy isolation.
[01:10] Maya: and for encryption and audit logs? we need at least SOC2 and audit trails, and keys managed by us ideally.
[01:17] Jordan: we have SOC 2 attestation in our security pack and the Private setup supports customer KMS integration; Dedicated also has stronger audit retention options. we'll send the security pack link after.
[01:26] Noah: can you clarify how caching works on hosted? sometimes our prompts share a lot of prefix so caching would be helpful.
[01:32] Priya: yes we have prefix/KV cache in the runtime — that helps reduce token costs and latency, but note it's best-effort on hosted; Dedicated gives you more control over cache policies.
[01:42] Liam: walk me through the quickstart steps if we go self-serve. we have a few engineers who can get it going.
[01:47] Jordan: step one sign up, claim credits, create an API key, and call /v1/generate (or chat endpoint). we have SDKs and a one-page quickstart with curl and python snippets. step two is load some prompts, test sample traffic. step three is if you need more performance we can provision dedicated seats or discuss a private plane.
[02:05] Maya: what's the typical amount of credits given for evaluation?
[02:08] Jordan: we usually give a small token allotment equivalent to a couple hundred thousand tokens; if you need more for a proper eval we'll extend it based on the pilot scope.
[02:17] Noah: how do you measure cost? is it per-token for generation and per-embed for embeddings? we have a classifier flow too.
[02:22] Jordan: yes per-token for generation, embeddings per call; we'll attach a simple cost calculator and an example spreadsheet.
[02:29] [Speaker 1]: uh hm (background)
[02:30] Priya: for your latency targets, we can run a quick benchmark using your prompt set — two configs: hosted baseline and a small dedicated reservation. that bench will give p50/p95 latency and per-token cost so you can decide.
[02:43] Liam: perfect, how invasive is that? we can't share production data but i can anonymize prompts.
[02:47] Priya: anonymized prompts are fine, we just need representative payloads and expected concurrency. we can run on our hosted cluster and optionally spin a small dedicated test if you want the numbers.
[02:57] Maya: what's the security review cadence? if we later want Private for compliance, how long does that process take?
[03:03] Jordan: Private/VPC deployments typically have a longer lead time — few weeks to set up depending on networking and KMS. that's why teams often start with hosted self-serve to validate product-market fit then move to Dedicated/Private when they need SLA and residency.
[03:18] Noah: are there any gotchas we should watch for when starting self-serve to avoid surprises on cost or latency?
[03:23] Priya: yes a couple: 1) model selection matters — a bigger model increases tokens & latency; 2) sequence length costs scale with prompt size; 3) cold-start tails — hosted is optimized but dedicated can tighten tails; 4) overuse of high-temp sampling can increase token spend.
[03:40] Liam: ok, so next steps would be: you run a small bench, we provide prompts, and you send pricing & security docs.
[03:46] Jordan: exactly — i'll send the pricing sheet and the credits redemption link today. priya will follow up on the bench plan and required artifacts.
[03:55] Maya: and please add the KMS and audit log section to the pack so we can share with our compliance folks.
[03:59] Priya: will do; we'll also include a short checklist outlining what's different between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
[04:07] Liam: curious — have you seen customers move from hosted to dedicated often? what's the tipping point?
[04:12] Jordan: usually it's predictability and cost at scale or regulatory needs — teams at sustained higher qps or with strict data controls move to Dedicated or Private. another tipping point is when they start running heavy embeddings or reranking workloads where consistency matters.
[04:28] Noah: any mention of competitor tradeoffs? we've looked at OpenAI for ease of use and Anthropic for safety, how do you compare?
[04:35] Priya: high-level: OpenAI has strong simplicity and model family; Anthropic focuses on alignment; our focus is serving and predictable economics across hosting options — so the difference is less about model correctness and more about how you run models at scale.
[04:52] [00:45] Speaker 2: (unintelligible)
[04:55] Jordan: i'll drop links to the security pack, the quickstart guide, and a sample benchmark plan.
[05:00] Maya: great. one last question on rollouts — we might want canary vs full rollout for model changes. how does Redwood support that?
[05:06] Priya: we support canary and A/B style rollouts with traffic split policies, and automatic rollback based on errors or latency thresholds. that's part of the console features.
[05:17] Liam: okay sounds good, let's aim to reconvene after the bench results.
[05:20] Jordan: perfect — thanks everyone.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
